question: What is the documentation difference between engineering judgment and an engineering study in the MUTCD definitions?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The evidence provided does not include the actual MUTCD definitions of "engineering judgment" and "engineering study" (typically found in Section 1D.03), so the definitional documentation difference cannot be fully stated from this evidence. What the available text does show is that a deviation from a Standard provision requires a "documented engineering study," whereas deviations from Guidance provisions may be justified by either engineering judgment or an engineering study — implying that formal documentation is tied to the engineering study, not to engineering judgment. Beyond this inference, the evidence is insufficient to state the full definitional distinction. Standards (mandatory): - "In limited, location-specific cases, the results of a documented engineering study (see Section 1D.03) might indicate a deviation from one or more requirements of a Standard provision to be appropriate." — for Standards, deviation is linked specifically to a documented engineering study. - For Guidance statements: "a statement of recommended practice in typical situations, with deviations allowed if engineering judgment or engineering study (see Section 1D.03) indicates the deviation to be appropriate." — either mechanism suffices, and no documentation is expressly stated. - "Those decisions shall be made using engineering judgment or engineering study, as required by the MUTCD provision." — decisions must be made by (or under the supervision of) an engineer with appropriate experience and expertise. - "The use of warning signs shall be based on an engineering study or on engineering judgment." — an example of a provision permitting either mechanism. Citations: - Section 1C.01 Standard §1 (p.13) - Section 1A.04 Standard §2 (p.2) - Section 2C.01 Standard §1 (p.147)
gold_answer: Both involve evaluating pertinent information and applying engineering principles by a professional engineer or a person under such an engineer's supervision. Engineering judgment does not require documentation; an engineering study must be documented in writing.
